texts.bodyNapsA: Short daytime naps of 10 to 20 minutes can restore alertness without leaving you groggy. Longer naps let you slip into deep sleep, and waking from it brings sleep inertia. Napping late in the afternoon can make it harder to fall asleep at night, so earlier is usually better.
texts.bodyNapsB: A brief nap of around 15 to 20 minutes tends to refresh you without grogginess. Sleep longer and you reach deep sleep, and waking then leaves you foggy. Napping late in the day often pushes back your bedtime, so aim for early afternoon.
